name: Warm Pink
lede: Warm Pink is a vivid, slightly red-leaning pink from the xkcd color survey of 2010, built by stacking the modifier "warm" onto the base color [[pink]].

sections.title: A modifier, not a story
sections.body: The name follows the same grammar as other crowd-survey names in our data: "warm" plus the base word [[pink]], rather than a plant, place or person [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 system's nearest block is deep pink, about six units from that block's center, so the official chip category reads it as deeper than the plain word "pink" alone would suggest [1]. Its closest measured look-alike is [[rosy-pink|Rosy Pink]], read as duller, with [[fiery-rose|Fiery Rose]] a little further out, read as redder, and [[medium-pink|Medium Pink]] further still, read as purpler and duller [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has this color covering at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [2]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole: a 2010 crowd-survey name has no particular reason to match an older painter's palette, and screen pinks this saturated are rare even among modern colors in centuries-old paintings [2].
